notes: Fixtures live in ./fixtures/. Subagents can't nest in the eval harness, so the generation subagent's work (Step B) runs INLINE by the eval-running agent. Atlassian, gh (OpenSpecResolver) and Allure TestOps are SIMULATED (no reachable MCP/repo in the eval env) — but skills/testplan/scripts/validate_test_plan.py runs for REAL against the generated test-plan.md and fixture spec.md, and its real exit code/output is what assertions are checked against. The Figma MCP is likewise SIMULATED: fixtures/figma-story/design-context.md stands in for get_screenshot + get_design_context, and the 'Figma down' run simply withholds it.

evals.name: openspec-grounded-context-enrichment
evals.prompt: Given fixtures/openspec-grounded/spec.md (two scenario'd requirements + one scenario-less 'Token rate limiting') plus the Story's acceptance criteria, generate test-plan.md per generation.md + test-plan-format.md (generation inline), then run validate_test_plan.py with --openspec pointing at the fixture spec.
evals.expected_output: Every case is grounded in an AC (source: ac: AC-<n>) and the OpenSpec scenarios ride only as openspec-ref: enrichment; the scenario-less requirement appears as a ## Gaps line; ## Conflicts is present (empty); validate_test_plan.py exits 0 with RESULT: PASS and scenario-coverage reports an advisory count, never a failure.

assertions.text: Every case's source: is 'ac: AC-<n>' (an AC listed in ## Acceptance Criteria) or 'QA-added: <reason>' — no case uses source: scenario:
Each OpenSpec scenario that shaped a case is cited as that case's openspec-ref: <Requirement>/<Scenario>, exact string match against the spec headings
The scenario-less 'Token rate limiting' requirement is named in a ## Gaps ⚠️ GAP line (not silently dropped)
The plan contains a ## Conflicts section header (empty is fine) and a ## Acceptance Criteria section
validate_test_plan.py was actually executed against the generated plan and fixture spec (not self-checked only)
validate_test_plan.py exits 0 and prints RESULT: PASS; scenario-coverage is reported as an advisory count and does not gate the outcome

evals.name: business-only-ac-coverage
evals.prompt: No service repo resolves and there is no OpenSpec file. Using only a Jira Story + PRD (acceptance criteria AC-1, AC-2), generate a business-only test-plan.md and validate WITHOUT --openspec.
evals.expected_output: The plan has a ## Acceptance Criteria section and a ## Conflicts header; every AC is covered by >=1 case with source: ac: AC-<n>; the header records openspec: none (<reason>); validate_test_plan.py (no --openspec) exits 0, scenario-coverage and gap-honesty report n/a.

assertions.text: Every AC-<n> in ## Acceptance Criteria is cited by >=1 case source: ac: AC-<n>
No case uses source: scenario: or source: design: — sources are ac: or QA-added: only
The header records openspec: none (<reason>) — the 'openspec:' spelling, not 'specs:'
The plan contains a ## Conflicts section header (may be empty)
validate_test_plan.py without --openspec exits 0 with RESULT: PASS; scenario-coverage and gap-honesty show n/a

evals.name: qa-lens-adds-negative
evals.prompt: For an acceptance criterion whose OpenSpec scenario implies a boundary/auth failure (break-glass), apply generation.md rule 2 and add a negative/edge case, then validate.
evals.expected_output: Beyond the base functional case, >=1 case tagged type: negative or type: edge exists, its boundary implied by the AC and the enriching OpenSpec scenario's WHEN/THEN, still using a business source: ac: AC-<n>. Validator exits 0.

assertions.text: A type: negative or type: edge case exists beyond the happy-path case
Its boundary/invalid input is implied by the acceptance criterion and the enriching OpenSpec scenario text, not fabricated
It uses source: ac: AC-<n> (business grounding), not QA-added: as an escape hatch, and any spec grounding rides as openspec-ref:
validate_test_plan.py exits 0

evals.name: no-fabrication-gap-honesty
evals.prompt: The spec has a scenario-less requirement ('Token rate limiting'). Confirm no case is invented for it and it is marked as a gap; validate.
evals.expected_output: No case cites 'Token rate limiting'; it appears once as a ## Gaps ⚠️ GAP line with an em dash and a reason; validate_test_plan.py gap-honesty PASS.

assertions.text: No ### TC- case is invented for the scenario-less requirement
'Token rate limiting' appears as a ## Gaps ⚠️ GAP: <req> — <reason> line (em dash U+2014)
No case carries an openspec-ref: naming the scenario-less requirement
validate_test_plan.py gap-honesty check PASS

evals.name: idempotent-upsert-key-stable
evals.prompt: Simulate two Step E runs over the SAME approved plan via testops_payload.traceability_tag + a simulated testops_find_testcases. Show the second run updates, not duplicates.
evals.expected_output: For each case, traceability_tag(story, service, capability, source, title, case_type) is identical across both runs; run 1 (find returns none) => create; run 2 (find returns the id) => update; no case is created twice. Tags are exactly qa-generated plus the tp- traceability tag and nothing else; type-*, priority-*, openspec-context, design-backed and spec-derived are all retired and never emitted.

assertions.text: traceability_tag is called with its real six-argument signature (story, service, capability, source, title, case_type) and is byte-identical for the same case across the two runs
Run 2's find (aql tags = the same tp- tag) matches run 1's created case, so the action is update
No case results in two create calls (0 duplicates)
The tp- tag is AQL-safe ([a-z0-9-]+) and present in the payload tags
Every payload's tags are exactly the tp- tag plus qa-generated — two tags, no more
No payload emits a retired tag: spec-derived, openspec-context, design-backed, type-* or priority-*

evals.name: dry-run-writes-nothing
evals.prompt: Run Step E with --dry-run over the approved plan. Confirm no create/update is issued and a per-case preview is printed.
evals.expected_output: Per testops-sync.md --dry-run: for each case, print intended action (create|update), its tp- tag, and payload name; issue ZERO testops_create_testcase / testops_update_testcase calls.

assertions.text: Zero create/update TestOps calls are issued under --dry-run
A per-case line prints the intended action, the tp- tag, and the payload name

evals.name: openspec-contradicts-business-holds
evals.prompt: fixtures/openspec-conflict/ holds a Story (story.md) whose AC-2 says a correct password while an account is LOCKED is refused with HTTP 423 and leaves the account locked, and an OpenSpec spec.md whose scenario 'A correct password clears the lock' says the opposite. Generate test-plan.md per generation.md + test-plan-format.md (generation inline), run validate_test_plan.py with --openspec spec.md, then append '→ resolved: business wins' to the conflict, regenerate the contradicted AC's case from the winning source, and run the validator again.
evals.expected_output: Run 1: no case is generated for the contradicted AC-2; a '⚠️ CONFLICT: AC-2 · story: … vs openspec: … — …' line names both sides; the validator exits 2 and prints 'RESULT: HOLD' naming that unresolved conflict. Run 2 (the same plan annotated '→ resolved: business wins', with AC-2's case now generated from the winning business source so it asserts the 423 refusal): the validator exits 0 with RESULT: PASS.

assertions.text: Any case that does exist takes its expected: from the acceptance criterion, never from the contradicting OpenSpec scenario
Run 1's plan contains NO ### TC- case citing source: ac: AC-2 — a contradicted AC yields no case at all
A '- ⚠️ CONFLICT: AC-2 · <source-a>: <claim> vs <source-b>: <claim> — <consequence>' line exists naming both the story and the openspec side (em dash U+2014 before the consequence)
The plugin picks no winner: run 1's plan contains no '→ resolved:' annotation anywhere
validate_test_plan.py on run 1 exits 2 and prints 'RESULT: HOLD', echoing the unresolved conflict line
Run 1 does NOT fail ac-coverage on the contradicted AC-2 (the exempt path), and the OpenSpec scenario the conflict names needs no ## Gaps line while the conflict is unresolved

After '→ resolved: business wins' is annotated and AC-2's case is regenerated from the winning business source (expected: the 423 refusal, not the spec's lock-clearing), validate_test_plan.py exits 0 with RESULT: PASS

evals.name: sot-precedence-is-documented
evals.prompt: Without generating any plan, read skills/testplan/SKILL.md and skills/testplan/references/*.md and report, quoting the exact lines, where the source-of-truth precedence is stated and whether any reference doc still calls OpenSpec files part of the source of truth. This is a documentation check: answer only from the files on disk, with grep-able quotes.
evals.expected_output: SKILL.md's '## Source of truth' section and generation.md's '## Precedence (read this first)' section both name the Jira Story + Confluence PRD + linked Figma mockup as the authoritative tier and OpenSpec spec.md files as supporting context only, with an explicit never-decide-`expected` rule; no reference doc lists OpenSpec files in the source of truth.

assertions.text: SKILL.md contains a '## Source of truth' section naming the Jira Story, the Confluence PRD and a Figma mockup linked from the Story as the authoritative tier
SKILL.md states OpenSpec spec.md files are supporting context only and that they may shape preconditions and steps but never a case's expected
generation.md opens with a '## Precedence (read this first)' section stating the Story/PRD/mockup decide what a case asserts and OpenSpec files only enrich
generation.md contains the never-override rule in so many words: OpenSpec text 'may never decide expected'
Both files state there is no precedence between Story, PRD and mockup inside the authoritative tier, and that a contradiction becomes a ## Conflicts line rather than a chosen expected

grep across skills/testplan/SKILL.md and skills/testplan/references/*.md finds NO sentence placing OpenSpec/spec files in the source of truth or the authoritative tier (every 'source of truth' mention lists Story/PRD/mockup only)
Both files state that a Confluence PRD/HLD is never called a 'spec' in this plugin
No reference doc still documents 'source: scenario:' or 'source: design:' as an accepted source kind (test-plan-format.md's migration note may only name them as the rejected old shape)

evals.name: figma-mockup-is-a-business-requirement
evals.prompt: fixtures/figma-story/story.md links a Figma frame and states only AC-1; fixtures/figma-story/design-context.md is a SIMULATED Figma design context (the eval env has NO Figma MCP — read that file instead of calling Figma) describing a 'Notifications · Empty state' frame the Story never mentions. Run 1: generate test-plan.md per generation.md + test-plan-format.md (generation inline) treating the mockup as a business requirement, and run validate_test_plan.py (no --openspec). Run 2: repeat with the Figma MCP simulated as unreachable — no design context at all — and validate again.
evals.expected_output: Run 1: the mockup's empty state is written into ## Acceptance Criteria as a new AC-<n> (an added detail, not a conflict); its case cites source: ac: AC-<n> and carries design-ref: <fileKey>/<nodeId> — <frame name>; the header reads design: remote (simulated); the validator exits 0 with RESULT: PASS. Run 2: the header reads design: none (<reason>), no design-ref: appears, the mockup-only AC and its case are absent, and the validator still exits 0 with RESULT: PASS — an unreachable Figma degrades, it never hard-stops.

assertions.text: The empty state shown only in the mockup appears in ## Acceptance Criteria as its own AC-<n>, with the frame's real strings ("You're all caught up" / "New notifications will appear here.")
It is recorded as an added acceptance criterion, NOT as a ## Conflicts line — the mockup adds detail the Story omits rather than contradicting it
The case covering that AC uses source: ac: AC-<n> — no case anywhere uses a 'design:' source kind

That case carries a well-formed design-ref: <fileKey>/<nodeId> — <frame name> (em dash U+2014) matching the fileKey and node id from the simulated design context, and validate_test_plan.py's design-ref-valid check PASSes
Run 1's header carries a design: line naming the backend that answered (remote, simulated)
validate_test_plan.py on run 1 exits 0 with RESULT: PASS
Run 2 (Figma simulated as down) writes design: none (<reason>) in the header, emits no design-ref: on any case, and does not invent the mockup-only AC from nothing
validate_test_plan.py on run 2 exits 0 with RESULT: PASS — an unreachable Figma degrades the run, it is never a hard stop or a FAIL
No real Figma MCP call is made in either run; the simulated design context file is the only design input

evals.name: story-prd-mockup-contradict-no-precedence
evals.prompt: fixtures/business-conflict/ holds three EQUAL business sources that disagree on one behaviour: story.md says a download link is valid for 7 days, prd.md says an export file is retained for 24 hours, and design-context.md — a SIMULATED Figma design context (the eval env has NO Figma MCP; read that file instead of calling Figma) — shows an 'Export · Ready' frame whose helper text reads 'This link expires in 30 days.'. Run 1: generate test-plan.md per generation.md + test-plan-format.md (generation inline) and run validate_test_plan.py (no --openspec). Run 2: the ADDITION variant — story-addition.md plus design-context-addition.md, where the mockup only adds detail the Story omits (an 'Export · In progress' frame) and contradicts nothing; generate test-plan-addition.md and validate it.
evals.expected_output: Run 1: no case is generated for the contradicted AC-2; a single '⚠️ CONFLICT: AC-2 · story: … vs prd: … vs design: … — …' line names all three disagreeing sides with their artifact and states that no winner was picked; the validator exits 2 and prints 'RESULT: HOLD' echoing that conflict, with ac-coverage PASSing (AC-2 is exempt while the conflict is unresolved). Run 2: the mockup-only detail becomes an extra AC-2 whose case cites source: ac: AC-2 and carries a design-ref:, the ## Conflicts section is empty, and the validator exits 0 with RESULT: PASS.

assertions.text: Run 1's plan contains NO ### TC- case citing source: ac: AC-2 — a contradicted acceptance criterion yields no case at all, not a case built on one of the three sources

A single '- ⚠️ CONFLICT: AC-2 · <source>: <claim> vs <source>: <claim> vs <source>: <claim> — <consequence>' line names ALL THREE disagreeing sides with their artifact keyword (story, prd and design), each with its own claim (em dash U+2014 before the consequence)
The plugin picks no winner anywhere in run 1's plan: no '→ resolved:' annotation, and no AC, case or conflict text that asserts one of 7 days / 24 hours / 30 days as the correct retention
Story, PRD and mockup are treated as equal authoritative sources — the plan contains no statement of precedence between them (the mockup is not demoted to context the way an OpenSpec file is)
validate_test_plan.py on run 1 exits 2 and prints 'RESULT: HOLD', echoing the unresolved conflict line
Run 1 does NOT fail ac-coverage on the contradicted AC-2 — the check PASSes because an AC named by an unresolved conflict is exempt and carries no case

Run 2 (the ADDITION variant): the detail shown only in the mockup — the spinner labelled "Preparing your export…" beside a "Cancel export" action — appears in ## Acceptance Criteria as its own AC-<n>, whose case cites source: ac: AC-<n> and carries a well-formed design-ref: <fileKey>/<nodeId> — <frame name>
Run 2's ## Conflicts section is present and EMPTY — a source that merely ADDS detail the Story omits is an extra acceptance criterion, never a conflict
validate_test_plan.py on run 2 exits 0 with RESULT: PASS
No real Figma MCP call is made in either run; the simulated design context files are the only design input

evals.name: payload-matches-reference-shape
evals.prompt: fixtures/reference-shape/test-plan.md holds one case whose content is Allure TestOps case 12684 (project 1, KING-18454) written in the new test-plan.md grammar. TestOps is SIMULATED, but skills/testplan/scripts/plan_parser.py and skills/testplan/scripts/testops_payload.py are pure stdlib Python and must be RUN FOR REAL: parse the plan with parse_cases, build the body with case_to_payload(case, story='KING-18454', service='kinoa-in-app', capability='milestones-eligibility', custom_fields={'Suite': '[KING-18454] As an operator I want to have Eligibility checkboxes for Milestones in-app', 'Story': 'Template', 'Component': 'In-Apps', 'Feature': 'Milestones'}), and compare the resulting dict key by key with fixtures/reference-shape/expected-payload.json. Report any extra, missing or differing key. NOTE: expected-payload.json was produced by case_to_payload and then hand-verified literal by literal against references/allure-push.md and Allure TestOps case 12684, so it is a checked reference, not merely the builder's own output; never regenerate it from the builder without repeating that hand verification.
evals.expected_output: The built payload equals fixtures/reference-shape/expected-payload.json exactly — same set of top-level keys, same values: name without a TC-n prefix, description = the purpose sentence, precondition = both precondition statements newline-separated, expectedResult = the case-level expected, status 'Draft', workflow 'Manual Kinoa', issues = [{name: 'Kinoa-Allure', value: 'KING-18454'}], customFields = Suite/Story/Component/Feature in that order with Suite composed as '[KING-18454] <story title>' and Story a project category value, one expectedResultSteps entry per step, and tags = exactly ['qa-generated', 'tp-…']. No links key and no testLayer key anywhere.

assertions.text: case_to_payload was actually executed (real import of skills/testplan/scripts/testops_payload.py) against the case parsed from the fixture plan — the payload is built, not hand-written

The built payload's top-level key set is exactly the expected JSON's: name, description, precondition, expectedResult, status, workflow, issues, customFields, scenario, tags — no extra key and no missing key
payload['name'] == 'Collecting a non-final milestone does not change the eligibility counter' — the TC-n prefix is stripped, the name is the title alone

payload['description'] == the case's purpose sentence ('Verify eligibility is untouched while the player progresses through milestones before the last one.') and contains no source:/traceability:/story: machine dump
payload['precondition'] carries BOTH precondition statements, newline-separated, exactly as the expected JSON has them — a continuation line is not dropped
payload['expectedResult'] == the case-level expected: line
payload['status'] == 'Draft' and payload['workflow'] == 'Manual Kinoa'
payload['issues'] == [{'name': 'Kinoa-Allure', 'value': 'KING-18454'}] and the payload has NO 'links' key

payload['customFields'] is the four {name, value} entries Suite, Story, Component, Feature in that order; Suite == '[KING-18454] As an operator I want to have Eligibility checkboxes for Milestones in-app' (composed from the key and the story title) and Story == 'Template' (a project category value, not the Jira story)

Every entry of payload['scenario']['steps'] is {'type': 'body', 'body': <action without its number>, 'expectedResultSteps': [{'type': 'expected_body', 'body': <result>}]} with exactly ONE expected_body per step, in plan order
payload['tags'] == ['qa-generated', 'tp-king-18454-kinoa-in-app-milestones-eligibility-b414d1aeef'] — exactly two tags, and no type-*, priority-*, openspec-context, design-backed or spec-derived tag
The payload has no 'testLayer' key at any level
The diff against fixtures/reference-shape/expected-payload.json is empty — the comparison is reported as equal, not 'close enough'

evals.name: unknown-custom-field-value-aborts-the-push
evals.prompt: Step E's Gate 0 pre-flight. Allure TestOps is SIMULATED, but skills/testplan/scripts/testops_fields.py is pure stdlib Python and must be RUN FOR REAL. Call check_field_values(fields={'Suite': '[KING-18454] As an operator I want to have Eligibility checkboxes for Milestones in-app', 'Story': 'Template', 'Component': 'In-App Templates', 'Feature': 'Milestones'}, lookups={'Story': {'totalElements': 32}, 'Component': {'content': [], 'totalElements': 0}, 'Feature': {'totalElements': 7}}, project_name='KINOA') — the simulated by-value lookup for the Component value 'In-App Templates' returned ZERO hits, i.e. that value does not exist in the project. Then carry out Step E as testops-sync.md describes, reporting every TestOps create/update call you would issue.
evals.expected_output: check_field_values returns ok=False with exactly one error naming the field and the offending value — "Component 'In-App Templates' does not exist in project KINOA — create it in Allure or pass an existing value" — and checked=['Story','Component','Feature'] (Suite is never looked up). Step E aborts at Gate 0: ZERO testops_create_testcase and ZERO testops_update_testcase calls are issued, and the abort message names the field and the value.

assertions.text: check_field_values was actually executed (real import of skills/testplan/scripts/testops_fields.py), not simulated by hand
It returns ok=False — a zero-hit lookup is treated as 'the value does not exist', never as 'unknown, proceed anyway'
The error names BOTH the field ('Component') and the offending value ('In-App Templates'), and the project name
checked == ['Story', 'Component', 'Feature'] — Suite is never looked up, because Allure creates Suite values on the fly
Story and Feature, whose lookups returned >=1 hit, produce no error — only the zero-hit value is rejected
ZERO testops_create_testcase calls and ZERO testops_update_testcase calls are issued: the abort happens at Gate 0, before any write
The run reports the abort to the user naming the offending field and value, rather than silently pushing and letting Allure fail the whole creation
